title: One delayed order. A clearer next step.
scenarioLabel: Illustrative scenario · fictional people and product · Concept UI

evidence.claim: Aster and all depicted capabilities are fictional examples for this template.
evidence.source: Authored illustrative scenario; not a real product or customer claim.

scenes.headline: “Where is my order?”
scenes.body: It is 9:14. Maya needs order #1842 for an event tomorrow. Her message lands with Tim.

cards.label: Customer message
cards.detail: “Can you tell me whether it will arrive?”

cards.label: Tim’s next move
cards.detail: He needs a current delivery status before making a promise.

scenes.narration: Meet Tim. A customer needs an order tomorrow. Before he can help, he needs to know what happened.
scenes.question: What would Tim check first in your team?
scenes.notes: Ask the buyer where delivery updates live today. Do not imply this is their current process.

scenes.headline: One case. The pieces beside it.
scenes.body: In this imagined workflow, Aster puts the order, latest carrier event and conversation in the same case.

cards.label: Order #1842
cards.detail: The latest update has no confirmed delivery date.

cards.label: Customer context
cards.detail: Maya has explained why timing matters.

cards.label: Decision needed
cards.detail: Tim has context. He still owns the next step.

scenes.narration: Now imagine Tim seeing the order, carrier update and customer conversation together. The delivery date is still unconfirmed.
scenes.question: Which piece of context is hardest to find today?
scenes.notes: Concept capability only. Replace with verified product evidence and real capture before using for a prospect.

scenes.headline: Give Tim a useful choice.
scenes.body: Tim can ask fulfillment about an alternative before promising Maya a replacement. Explore how his next move changes the handoff.
scenes.visualLabel: Concept UI / choose a next step

cards.label: Known
cards.detail: The original shipment has a carrier delay.

cards.label: Available action
cards.detail: Request an availability check with the case attached.

scenes.narration: Tim can ask fulfillment about an alternative, with the case already attached. He does not promise a replacement before it is checked.
scenes.question: Where should a person stay in control?
scenes.notes: Discuss approval boundaries. These are illustrative alternatives, not actual product automation.

choices.label: Check an alternative
choices.result: Fulfillment receives an availability check with order #1842 and the deadline attached.

choices.label: Request a carrier update
choices.result: The case stays with Tim while he asks for a current carrier update. No delivery date is promised.

scenes.headline: The context travels with the case.
scenes.body: The fulfillment teammate receives order #1842, the event deadline and Tim’s question together.

cards.label: Attached context
cards.detail: Carrier delay · event tomorrow · customer conversation

cards.label: Requested check
cards.detail: Confirm stock and delivery options before replying.

cards.label: Customer update
cards.detail: Tim tells Maya what he is doing, without inventing a date.

scenes.narration: The next teammate receives the order, the deadline and the question together. Tim can tell Maya what is being checked.
scenes.question: What would the next teammate need to act?
scenes.notes: Do not claim reduced handling time. The observable change is a context-bearing request.

scenes.headline: A clearer answer starts here.
scenes.body: Maya has an honest update. Fulfillment has a specific request. Tim knows what he is waiting for.
scenes.narration: Maya has an honest update. Fulfillment has a specific request. Where would this kind of handoff help your team?
scenes.question: Which of your team’s handoffs would you put in this story?
scenes.notes: Invite correction and choose a real scenario for a capture-backed version.
